topic: No-solution linear system with a parameter
problem: 6 + 7r = pw and 7r - 5w = 5w + 11. In this system of equations, p is a constant. If the system has no solution, what is the value of p?

bad.why: Making the two equations identical gives the same line (infinitely many solutions), the opposite of no solution.

algebraFirst.description: Solves both equations for w, sets the slopes 7/p and 7/10 equal to get p=10, and often skips checking that the lines are distinct rather than the same line.

explanationNotes: Explain 'no solution' as 'two parallel lines that never touch'. Rename r as x and w as y so Desmos can graph both equations as written, drag p until the lines are parallel (p=10), and point out they are two separate lines, not one line drawn twice (that would mean infinitely many solutions).
notes: Rewrite as w=(6+7r)/p and w=(7r-11)/10. A method that only matches slopes (derivative regression alone) checks a necessary but not sufficient condition, since matching slopes is equally satisfied by two coincident lines (infinitely many solutions). Both original equations must be graphed at the fitted p to confirm the lines are parallel and distinct, not coincident.
